comparison: Both evaluate methodological claims (C21-C32) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on documentation of sample collection and participant characteristics. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the 'sophisticated near-full length sequencing technique' and describe the study as 'technically demanding and here is well done.' Both affirm the methodological rigor, though peer review extends evaluation to include some sequencing results (C33-C36).

OpenEval evaluates sequencing results (C33-C39) as SUPPORTED with focus on quantitative data and clonality. Peer review R1 includes some of these claims (C33-C36) in their broader methodological affirmation but does not separately evaluate the intact provirus proportion or clonality findings detailed in C37-C39.

Both address intact provirus findings. OpenEval R2 evaluates C37-C39 (sequencing results including 3.21% intact proviruses) as SUPPORTED. Peer R2 evaluates overlapping claims C37-C39 plus tissue distribution claims (C40-C43, C48, C145) as SUPPORTED, with editor stating results are 'convincing.' Agreement on intact provirus data quality.

Partial overlap on tissue distribution of intact proviruses. OpenEval R3 evaluates C40-C50 (tissue distribution with CNS focus) as SUPPORTED but notes small sample size limits generalizability. Peer R2 includes C40-C43, C48 in their SUPPORTED evaluation of intact provirus findings across anatomical sites. Both accept the data but OpenEval more explicitly qualifies limitations.

Both address CNS intact provirus findings. OpenEval R3 evaluates C40-C50 including novelty claim (C50) as SUPPORTED with qualification about sample size. Peer R3 evaluates C44-C47, C49-C50, C99-C100, C146 as SUPPORTED, with reviewers explicitly affirming CNS findings as 'relevant for understanding latent viral reservoirs, especially in the brain.' Strong agreement on CNS reservoir significance.

High concordance on defective provirus distribution (C51-C57). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes high prostate frequencies and low CNS frequencies as data-driven conclusions from Figure 2C. Peer review accepts these findings without challenge, with editor's statement about proviruses at 'various anatomical sites' implicitly accepting the distribution patterns. Peer R4 also includes C126 (prostate findings).

Strong agreement on clonality patterns (C58-C65). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes multi-tissue distribution and CNS-lymphoid connections documented in Figures 3A-C. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm clonality findings, with one noting importance of understanding 'how clones of infected T cells can move around the body, including into the CNS compartment.' Peer R5 also includes summary claims C101-C102, C147.

Strong agreement on CNS clonality (C66-C77). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval documents specific examples from each participant with qualification about small sample size limiting generalization strength. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'They identified clonally expanded proviruses in the CNS in all three individuals' as a key finding and describe results as 'convincing.' Peer R6 also includes summary claims C103-C104, C148.

Significant disagreement on viral tropism analysis (C78-C85). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED but notes tropism relies on computational prediction rather than functional validation. Peer review evaluates as UNCERTAIN, with reviewer raising concern that 'there is another entry phenotype beyond X4' and emphasizing need to understand macrophage-tropic viruses in CNS. Peer review identifies incomplete analysis that OpenEval accepts with mild qualification.

Perfect agreement on negative findings (C86-C87). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes findings are appropriately qualified and consistent with suppressive ART. Peer reviewers accept without challenge, consistent with clinical adherence data. Complete concordance.

Both address CNS findings but different aspects. OpenEval R9 evaluates C99-C104 (CNS synthesis claims) as SUPPORTED with qualification that 'preferential persistence' in basal ganglia may be overstated. Peer R3 includes C99-C100 in broader SUPPORTED evaluation of CNS reservoir significance. OpenEval more critical of specific localization claims.

Both address participant 2's clinical history and tropism (C118-C125). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED but notes speculation about relationship between R5 adaptation and lack of intact CNS proviruses. Peer R7 evaluates broader tropism claims as UNCERTAIN, emphasizing need to understand macrophage-tropic viruses. Peer review more skeptical of tropism interpretations overall.

Both address prostate reservoir findings. OpenEval R11 evaluates C126-C130 as SUPPORTED, acknowledging limitation about cell type identification and speculation about myeloid involvement. Peer R4 includes C126 in SUPPORTED evaluation of defective provirus distribution without specific challenge to prostate findings or cell type uncertainty.

Both address cell type identification limitations. OpenEval R11 evaluates C126-C130 including cell type limitation (C128) and myeloid speculation (C129) as SUPPORTED. Peer R9 evaluates C128-C129 (among other cell type claims) as UNCERTAIN, with reviewer explicitly stating 'Cell type identification would greatly enhance the impact of this work.' Peer review more emphatic about this limitation.

Strong agreement on study limitations (C131-C141). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes limitations are appropriately acknowledged and blood contamination argument is logical but not definitive. Peer reviewers explicitly emphasize these limitations, particularly small sample size (n=3), clinical characteristics of participants, and possibility of blood infiltration. Both recognize importance of these caveats for interpretation.

OpenEval R13 evaluates background/context claims (C88-C97) about HIV-1 CNS invasion as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and qualifications. No corresponding peer review evaluation found that specifically addresses these background claims, though peer reviewers implicitly accept the contextual framework.

Disagreement on cell type hypotheses (C105-C117). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN, noting hypotheses are reasonable with appropriate citations but remain speculative without cell-type identification data. Peer R9 also evaluates as UNCERTAIN but is more emphatic, with reviewers explicitly stating 'it is unclear which cell types these viruses persist in' and that 'Cell type identification would greatly enhance the impact.' Both recognize uncertainty but peer review emphasizes this as a more significant limitation.

Agreement on study contributions and implications (C142-C149). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes conclusions about tissue distribution are well-supported and cure strategy implications are reasonable though somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers affirm study as 'important' and 'well done,' contributing to understanding of tissue distribution and informing viral eradication efforts. Both recognize value while acknowledging speculative elements about future impact.
